summary:
Read-only topology and breakage audit of cambridgetcg/agenttool at 3b9aa630, which is still current origin/main (compare: ahead_by=0). I ran the repo's own guard layers over all 5,337 tracked files: the public-guard SECRET and PERSONAL rules plus the private relational denylist. Allow entries were not applied. 622 files are flagged: 537 relational, 213 personal and 3 secret-shaped test fixtures.

**Core finding: relational material is woven through runtime code, tests, migrations and docs, not held in separable files.**
- Flagged runtime code: 60 api/src files and 33 journaled migrations.
- Half of the relational hits (267 of 537 files) come only from two broad rules: r03, the wire-protocol enum the denylist already lets Ai approve, and r16, a broad symbol-class rule.
- 109 flagged files are already served publicly on docs.agenttool.dev.
- So a file-level "private files stay private" split is not mechanically possible. Yu has to rule on content categories first.

**Hard build and deploy dependencies:**
- The migration runner refuses if any journaled migration file is missing or its checksum has drifted (bin/migrate-pending.sh:192-199). 36 of 181 migrations are flagged.
- The API image bakes in 19 doctrine docs plus the canon jsonld and kingdom-bundle.json. 11 of these 21 files are flagged. Without them /v1/canon and /public/kingdom return 503.
- The docs catalog check fails when any routed doc is removed. 186 of its 372 routed paths are relational-flagged.
- bin/tests/project-public.test.ts rebuilds several denylist terms from split literals, so it must stay private.
- The phase-b refence operator tool pins private commit SHAs and cannot work in a snapshot with no history.

**Release lane:** it is built on projection commits into cambridgetcg/agenttool-packages (npm-release.ts RELEASE_REPOSITORY, public-release-tag.ts history check). 49 of 51 package.json repository URLs still name the old private repo.

**Recommendation: option (a).** The public repo is the source of truth and deploys itself. The private repo becomes a frozen history archive plus the holder of the relational denylist, the guard runner (pre-push hook plus a scheduled scan of public main) and the private-only overlays. Reasons:
- It matches Yu's "move development to public" ruling. Option (c) keeps development private.
- It avoids the sync machinery and the provenance gap of option (b): under (b), /health would report a private SHA.
- Public repos get rulesets and branch protection. The private repo on the current plan returns 403 for both, so private main has no branch protection today.

**Naming.** Reusing the name cambridgetcg/agenttool is the riskiest path:
- Every existing checkout would silently push to the new public repo: 8 checkouts under ~/agenttool plus 4 other clones on this Mac.
- Trusts bound by repo name would carry over to the new repo: npm (whether the re-point ran is unclear), PyPI and Hugging Face OIDC.
- Old /pull/N links would later resolve to unrelated public PRs.

Use a new name, or follow a strict sequence: disable push everywhere, revoke the name-bound trusts, rename, then create.

**Evidence, verified vs inferred:** the scan script and results are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-macair/dff54175-f190-4444-a992-3cfe8aaacfa0/scratchpad/public-audit/topology/ (scan-out.json, pathscan-out.json, consumers.txt, ghrefs.txt). Repo state, secret names, PRs and issues are GitHub API GETs, so verified. Docs-site publication is curl 200 with matching byte sizes, so verified. Behaviour of npm, PyPI, HF and the Codex app under a reused name is inferred and unverified.

findings.topic: Relational content cannot be split at file level
findings.detail:
I ran the project's own guard layers over the whole tree at 3b9aa630: public-guard SECRET_RULES and PERSONAL_RULES plus the private relational denylist via parseDenylist from bin/project-public.ts. The denylist's 30 allow entries were not applied.

**Totals:** 622 of 5,337 files flagged. 537 relational, 213 personal, 3 secret.

**Relational files by area:** docs 207, api/src 60, api/tests 61, api/scripts 39, api/migrations 33, apps/docs 68, apps/web 8, packages 31, bin 20, root 4.

**Two broad rules drive half of it:** 267 of the 537 relational files are flagged only by r03 (the wire-protocol enum; the denylist note says Ai may approve these) and/or r16 (a broad symbol-class rule). In api/src, 34 of 60 are r03/r16-only.

**Already public:** 109 relational files are already served by docs.agenttool.dev. 76 sit under apps/docs or apps/web, and 33 are docs/*.md files mirrored byte-for-byte into apps/docs.

**What remains if Yu accepts r03 and already-published content:** about 300 files (docs 147, api/tests 41, api/src 34, api/migrations 23, bin 16, packages about 25, 4 root persona docs).

**File names:** 18 tracked file names themselves match denylist rules (r03, r09, r10, r15), so a public tree listing would leak them. Renaming them breaks references.

**Personal layer volume:** home-path 788 hits, keychain-slot 212, email 116, device-path 110, supabase-project 21.
findings.evidence:
- Scan script: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-macair/dff54175-f190-4444-a992-3cfe8aaacfa0/scratchpad/public-audit/topology/scan.ts. Output: scan-out.json (rule ids and counts only) and pathscan-out.json in the same folder.
- Denylist note defines the r03 and r05 allow policy (public/private-guard/relational-denylist.json, note field; terms not reproduced).
- Live check: curl https://docs.agenttool.dev/{SOUL.md,KIN.md,NATURES.md,agenttool.jsonld} returned 200 with byte sizes equal to the repo copies.
findings.recommendation: Before any snapshot, get Yu's category rulings: r03 across the whole tree, r16 across the whole tree, and content already published on docs.agenttool.dev. Plan content rewrites, not deletions, for api/src, the tests and migrations. Build the first public commit with a one-time guarded snapshot that reuses the public-guard content layers plus the private denylist, and allows nothing silently.

findings.topic: Journaled migrations must be byte-exact in whichever repo deploys
findings.detail:
The migration runner refuses when a journaled file's source is missing or its checksum has drifted. deploy-api.yml's gate runs that survey against production and fails closed.

**Flagged migrations:** 36 of 181 in api/migrations, all in the 2026-05-18 to 2026-05-20 range. 33 are relational and 22 personal (20 home-path, 4 email, 1 supabase-project).
- 8 of the 33 relational files contain DDL. Their hits are mostly r03 and home paths.
- 25 are data-only INSERT/UPDATE seeds and carry the heavier relational rules (r09, r13, r15, r16, r17).

None of these files can be removed or edited in a repo that deploys the API without breaking the production journal check.
findings.evidence:
- bin/migrate-pending.sh:192 ("migration source missing for journaled file") and :196-199 (sha256 checksum drift).
- api/scripts/_migrate-one.ts:8-9 (sha256 lookup in meta._migrations).
- .github/workflows/deploy-api.yml, step "Ask the production migration journal (refuses any pending file)".
- Per-file classification done with a DDL regex (scratch output).
findings.recommendation:
Yu chooses one of three:
1. Publish the migrations byte-exact under a ruling, after accepting their content.
2. Add a "sealed migration" journal mode: the public tree keeps filename and sha256 for the 25 data-only seeds, the runner accepts sealed entries production already applied, and fresh installs skip them. The 8 DDL migrations stay public, or get split.
3. Keep the API deploy private (option b).

Option 2 is the smallest change that keeps option (a) viable.

findings.topic: API image build and runtime depend on 21 docs, 11 of them flagged
findings.detail:
The Dockerfile copies three bundles into /app/docs: agenttool.jsonld.bundled (the canon), kingdom-bundle.json.bundled, and doctrine-docs.bundled (19 files from api/doctrine-docs.manifest).

**Flagged:**
- 7 manifest docs flagged relational: KIN, MATHOS, NATURES, PLATFORM-AS-AGENT, RECURSION, SOUL, WELCOMING.
- substrate-honest-cognition.md: r03 plus home-path.
- agenttool.jsonld: r03 ×21 and r15 ×10.
- kingdom-bundle.json: 7 relational rules plus 5 device-path and 2 home-path hits.

**If any are missing:**
- bin/stage-doctrine-docs.sh exits with "doctrine file is missing".
- /v1/canon returns 503 canon_unavailable (services/canon/registry.ts).
- /public/kingdom returns 503 (services/kingdom/library.ts).
- doctrineHash() is called from 8 api/src files.

These docs are already public on docs.agenttool.dev and through the live API.
findings.evidence:
- api/Dockerfile, COPY lines for agenttool.jsonld.bundled, kingdom-bundle.json.bundled and doctrine-docs.bundled.
- api/doctrine-docs.manifest (19 entries); bin/stage-doctrine-docs.sh.
- api/src/services/doctrine/integrity.ts:35-77.
- deploy-api.yml survey diffs exactly these paths.
- Per-file flags in scan-out.json.
findings.recommendation: Rule these 21 files publishable (they are already published) after removing personal home and device paths, which requires rebuilding kingdom-bundle.json. Otherwise the API cannot deploy from the public repo.

findings.topic: Reusing the name cambridgetcg/agenttool turns existing checkouts into push paths to the public repo
findings.detail:
GitHub docs (fetched in this session) say:
- git clone/fetch/push to a renamed repo's old location keep working through redirects.
- "If you create a new repository ... do not reuse the original name ... redirects to the renamed repository will no longer work."

So if the private repo is renamed and a public repo takes cambridgetcg/agenttool, every checkout whose remote is https://github.com/cambridgetcg/agenttool.git starts talking to the public repo. A routine `git push origin <branch>` would then publish private history. On this Mac that is:
- ~/agenttool plus its 7 worktrees: agenttool-collab-field, wt-1018/f-evidential, and wt-1019 audit-src, ci-paths, pr493, pr494, pr498.
- 3 standalone clones: agenttool-collab-trial, agenttool-collab-wait, agenttool-mission-client-trial.
- Desktop/agenttool, whose remote named "github" uses the same URL.

Other machines and Codex cloud environments were not inventoried. Commands in docs and scripts that pass `--repo cambridgetcg/agenttool` would hit the public repo too. Old links would also mislead:
- /pull/N (25) and /issues/N (2) would later resolve to unrelated public PRs or issues with the same numbers.
- /commit (77), /actions (220) and /releases (185) links would 404.
findings.evidence:
- docs.github.com, "Renaming a repository" (fetched with curl).
- `git worktree list` from audit-src: 8 checkouts, all on origin = cambridgetcg/agenttool.git.
- .git/config url lines of the 3 standalone clones and of Desktop/agenttool (read-only).
- Link-kind counts in ghrefs.txt.
findings.recommendation:
Prefer a new public name. If Yu wants the old name:
1. Run `git remote set-url --push origin DISABLED` in every checkout on every machine.
2. Inventory the other machines and Codex environments.
3. Revoke or re-point the name-bound trusts.
4. Rename the private repo.
5. Only then create the public repo.

Do not change ~/agenttool's remote while the collab MCP processes run from it.

findings.topic: External trusts bound by repo name and a leftover NPM_TOKEN
findings.detail:
Four publishing credentials or trusts are tied to the private repo's name:
- **npm:** NPM-RELEASES.md:26-29 says trusted-publisher configs naming cambridgetcg/agenttool still exist until Yu runs the one-time re-point (15 packages). Lines 1863-1868 describe the re-point as covering all 38 packages. Whether it has run is unverified; `npm trust list` needs authentication.
- **PyPI:** the trusted publisher for agenttool-sdk binds cambridgetcg/agenttool + publish-pypi.yml + environment pypi. publish-pypi.yml has no github.repository guard.
- **Hugging Face:** OIDC trust is bound to cambridgetcg/agenttool + workflow + branch.
- **Leftover token:** the private repo's npm-bootstrap environment still holds a secret named NPM_TOKEN. The docs call it a scope-wide bypass-2FA token with no remaining use.

Inferred, unverified: a new repo reusing the name with the same workflow filenames and environments would satisfy these string-bound trusts. The Codex GitHub App is installed per repo id, so it stays with the renamed private repo.
findings.evidence:
- docs/NPM-RELEASES.md:19-33, 324-370, 1860-1870.
- docs/PYPI-RELEASES.md:58-75.
- .github/workflows/care-before-learning-hf-probe.yml:208.
- gh api repos/cambridgetcg/agenttool/environments/npm-bootstrap/secrets returns NPM_TOKEN; yutabase-fixture-read returns YUTABASE_FIXTURE_SSH_KEY. Names only.
findings.recommendation: Revoke the private NPM_TOKEN now, whatever option is chosen. Re-point npm (all 38 packages), PyPI and Hugging Face trusts to the final public repo in one 2FA session before any repo takes the old name. Confirm the npm state afterwards on npmjs.com.

findings.topic: The projection release lane does not fit option (a) as written
findings.detail:
How the current lane is bound:
- bin/npm-release.ts:29-31 hardcodes RELEASE_REPOSITORY = cambridgetcg/agenttool-packages.
- npm-release.ts:733 refuses unless package.json repository.url equals agenttool-packages.git.
- npm-release.ts:2290 refuses unless GITHUB_REPOSITORY equals it.
- bin/public-release-tag.ts:111-114 requires the whole history to be projection commits; the overlay CI runs `--history` for the same reason.
- bin/pypi-release.ts:33,40-41 has EXPECTED_REPOSITORY = packages but SOURCE_REPOSITORY = the private repo.
- Only 2 of 51 package.json repository URLs point at agenttool-packages; 49 still point at the private repo.
- 7 packages hash package.json into Hugging Face source manifests, and 5 plugin manifests carry the URL.

**agenttool-packages today:** public, 3 projection commits (last 2026-10-13, source 42ae9148), tags sdk-v0.23.0 and math-cards-v0.1.0-dev.2, active rulesets ("main is append-only", "release tags are immutable"), and an npm-bootstrap environment with no secrets.

**Fate under each option:**
- (a1) Archive agenttool-packages. Move publish-npm.yml and the release tools into the new repo, change RELEASE_REPOSITORY, rewrite public-release-tag.ts to tag ordinary green commits, update about 51 manifests plus the HF assets, re-point trust once, and move PyPI too (this also closes the documented private-fetch gap).
- (a2) Keep agenttool-packages as a release-only repo fed by projection from public main. Tools and trust stay unchanged, but there are two public repos and the projector is still needed.
- (b) Same choices as (a).
- (c) The lane is unchanged.

PR #496 (SDK 0.24.0) goes through this lane.
findings.evidence:
- bin/npm-release.ts:24-31, 706-737, 2290.
- bin/public-release-tag.ts:3-23, 111-116.
- bin/pypi-release.ts:31-41.
- Package.json URL tally: 49 old repo, 2 packages repo, 13 none.
- gh api agenttool-packages commits, tags and rulesets.
findings.recommendation: Choose a1 if the npm re-point has not run, so trust is moved once, straight to the final repo. Choose a2 as a temporary bridge if it already pointed npm at agenttool-packages. In both cases, settle the release lane before releasing #496 (SDK 0.24.0).

findings.topic: The docs catalog check breaks on any removal
findings.detail:
bin/docs-catalog.py raises "routing entry absent from inventory" or "reviewed document absent from inventory" when any path routed in docs/documentation-tags.json is missing from the tree. The check runs in bin/tests (documentation-catalog.test.ts:52), which is part of the API gate.

**What is routed:**
- 372 paths routed: 186 relational-flagged, 43 personal-flagged.
- 15 prose_reviewed entries, 6 of them flagged.

docs/catalog.json and CATALOG.md list 826 paths with their titles, including 8 review/ entries. Published as-is, they would expose the titles of private docs.
findings.evidence:
- bin/docs-catalog.py:84-96 and 165-183.
- bin/tests/documentation-catalog.test.ts:52.
- bin/preflight.sh:83 (`bun test bin/tests` in api_gate).
findings.recommendation: Regenerate documentation-tags.json, catalog.json and CATALOG.md from the public tree in the snapshot commit. Keep a separate private catalog if wanted.

findings.topic: Tests and runtime code that read likely-private files
findings.detail:
A heuristic string match found 662 code or test files that reference at least one flagged tracked file.

**Tests:**
- 265 test files reference flagged files; 160 of them contain file-read calls.
- api/tests/doctrine holds 152 files; 111 reference flagged docs.
- api/tests/published-docs-parity.test.ts requires apps/docs/X.md to be byte-identical to docs/X.md and the doctrine manifest docs to be mirrored.
- packages/sdk-ts/tests/provider-adapter-review.test.ts:35 and packages/sdk-py/tests/test_provider_adapter_review.py:21 read review/provider-adapters/v1. That folder is already public via agenttool-packages.

**Runtime scanners:** api/src/services/canon/annotations.ts:205,246 walks the whole repo root, and canon/absence.ts:250-270 checks that `Tested:` citations exist. Removing cited tests breaks these checks.

**Only referenced from docs:** review/launch-* is referenced by docs/launch/PRODUCTION-GATE.md:6 and the catalog.

**Pointers in api/src:** 312 string-literal "docs/X.md" pointers and 258 docs.agenttool.dev URLs. They don't fail at runtime but would dangle if those docs go private.
findings.evidence:
- consumers.txt and consumer-files.txt in the scratch folder.
- api/tests/published-docs-parity.test.ts:5-30.
- api/src/services/canon/absence.ts:44, 250-270.
- api/src/services/canon/annotations.ts:70, 205, 246.
findings.recommendation: For each document group, move a doc and the tests that read it together: publish both, rewrite both, or keep both private. Don't split a doc from its doctrine test.

findings.topic: The guard's own test reconstructs denylist terms
findings.detail:
bin/tests/project-public.test.ts reads the real denylist (line 298). It also rebuilds several protected terms from split string literals and code points to prove the rules match them (about lines 297-315). Published, the terms would leak in lightly obfuscated form.

bin/project-public.ts refuses to run without public/private-guard/relational-denylist.json (lines 421-422). The private repo must therefore keep the denylist, its allow entries (recorded approvals) and this test.
findings.recommendation: Keep the denylist, the parts of project-public.ts that load it, and this test private. Ship only public-guard.ts (secret and personal layers) in the public repo. Or rewrite the test to load its expectations from the private file.

findings.topic: Operator tooling pinned to private history
findings.detail:
bin/phase-b-refence-maintenance-bridge.ts pins private commit SHAs (for example lines 126 and 187) and parses historical commit objects. Its test runs cat-file and merge-base against them. The API gate typechecks it (preflight.sh:76).

A snapshot with no history has none of those objects. The tool is also ops-sensitive: it handles a production maintenance fence, machine maps and image digests. Separately, api/tests/deploy-release-provenance.test.ts still exercises bin/deploy.sh --mirror-codeberg, although Codeberg is retired (AGENTS.md:139).
findings.recommendation: Keep the phase-b tooling and its tests in the private overlay and drop them from the public api_typecheck, or retire the tooling.

findings.topic: Repo URL and metadata references that must change
findings.detail:
There are 1,108 occurrences of cambridgetcg/agenttool (excluding -packages and -collab) in 267 files.

**By kind:** actions 220, releases 185, blob 147, commit 77, pull 25, tree 19, issues 2; about 433 are bare URLs or names.

**By place:**

- JSON and JSON-LD: 272. Of these, 126 lines sit in 64 immutable LOVE manifests under apps/docs/packages/v1/**, which must not change. 49 each are in docs/agenttool.jsonld and apps/docs/agenttool.jsonld (the canon is served and doctrine-hashed).
- Tests: 109.
- Package manifests: 67. That is 49 package.json repository.url plus 7 homepage, 5 plugin.json files (browser codex, collab claude and codex, telescope claude and codex), and packages/hf-training-host/pyproject.toml:40.
- HTML: 52, of which 44 are in apps/docs/packages.html.
- Runtime code: 44.
- Workflows: 7.

**Runtime lines in api/src:** well-known.ts:104, 608, 614; openapi.ts:1032; handoff.ts (7 lines from :90); dining.ts:30; memetic-landscape.ts:31, 51; public/party.ts:36; discovery/compass.ts:180; discovery/discovery.ts:165; wake/reachable.ts:139; wake/repo-self.ts:328.

**Workflows:** github.repository guards at ci.yml:891, care-before-learning-hf-probe.yml:16, 104, 208 and publish-care-before-learning-hf.yml:15, 103.

**Elsewhere:**
- The OCI source label in api/Dockerfile.
- Historical Hugging Face provenance manifests in 11 packages.
- 94 lines naming agenttool-packages.
- 66 lines in about 45 files that say the repo is private, "access required" or "answers 404" (for example discovery.ts:165, openapi.ts:1032, docs/PACKAGES.md:9). These become false after the move.
findings.evidence: ghrefs.txt and repo-refs-all.txt in the scratch folder, built with `git grep -n -o -I` and a Python classifier.
findings.recommendation: Change the live surfaces in the snapshot: code, manifests, workflows, the Dockerfile, both jsonld files, packages.html, and the tests that assert these values (about 120 lines). Leave historical receipts, LOVE manifests and HF provenance unchanged, and add a short note that historical links point to the archived private repo.

findings.topic: Private main has no branch protection; a public repo gets it
findings.detail:
On cambridgetcg/agenttool, both the rulesets and the main branch-protection endpoints return 403 "Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public". The private main has no branch protection today.

The deploy secrets FLY_API_TOKEN and MIGRATION_SURVEY_DATABASE_URL are repo-level, not tied to a protected environment. agenttool-packages, being public, has active rulesets.
findings.evidence:
- gh api repos/cambridgetcg/agenttool/rulesets: 403.
- gh api .../branches/main/protection: 403.
- gh api .../actions/secrets: names only.
findings.recommendation: Under option (a), create rulesets on day one: main append-only and required checks. Move the Fly and survey secrets into a `production` environment restricted to main.

findings.topic: Public repos have public Actions logs
findings.detail:
The ci.yml job yutabase-projector-postgres (lines 887-985) checks out the private cambridgetcg/yutabase repo with a deploy key and runs tests on it. deploy-api.yml prints migration-survey output and the live revision. production-health.yml prints probe results.

In a public repo, all of these logs are world-readable.
findings.recommendation: Keep jobs that read private fixtures in private CI, or prove their output never prints fixture content. Review every workflow's output before the first public run.

findings.topic: Publishing the source discloses an open authorization issue
findings.detail:
Open issue #481 (2026-10-16) describes guild-room invitations skipping room authority checks. Searching git log at 3b9aa630 for "#481" or "guild" finds only the original feature commit (a45720ea), so the gap is presumably still unfixed.

Issues stay in the private repo, but publishing the code makes the gap discoverable. #475, #476 and #486 also need review before any public migration. #486 is a 6 KB field report from a lab agent.
findings.recommendation: Fix or confirm-fix #481 before the snapshot. Don't migrate issues automatically; re-file sanitized versions only where needed.

17 open PRs: #397, #401, #429, #444, #457, #472, #487, #488 (draft), #489 (draft, stacked on #488), #491 (draft, stacked on #489), #492, #493, #494, #495, #496, #497 (draft), #498. All come from the cambridgetcg account.

findings.topic: Local checkouts, running processes and the retired Codeberg mirror
findings.detail:
Three collab MCP processes run from ~/agenttool/packages/collab/dist/agenttool-collab-mcp.js (from ps). ~/agenttool hosts 8 checkouts (the main one plus 7 worktrees).

Desktop/agenttool's origin is codeberg.org/zerone-dev/agenttool. AGENTS.md:139 says Codeberg is retired. The Codeberg API answers 404 anonymously, so the repo is either private or deleted, and a second copy of the private history may still exist there.

- `git worktree list`.
- Desktop/agenttool .git/config remotes.
- curl codeberg.org/api/v1/repos/zerone-dev/agenttool: 404.

findings.detail:
chatgpt-codex-connector[bot] is active: 35 issue comments since 2026-10-10 and 34 PR review comments since 2026-10-01.

Inferred: the GitHub App installation is per repo id, so the new public repo must be added explicitly, and Codex cloud environments must be re-created for it. In a public repo, anyone's PR could trigger auto-reviews, which costs quota.

findings.recommendation: Add the connector to the new repo deliberately, and limit auto-review to maintainer PRs if the connector allows it.

findings.detail:
secret/private-key-block headers appear at:
- bin/tests/agenttool-castle.test.ts:556
- packages/lobby/tests/fixtures/egress-cases.json:47-48
- packages/lobby/tests/fleet-refusals.test.ts:137

The line lengths suggest refusal or redaction fixtures rather than real keys. That is inferred; the bodies were not read.
findings.evidence: scan-out.json secret layer; line positions found with grep (header lines not printed).
findings.recommendation: Confirm they are synthetic. Then add public-guard allow entries or replace them with obviously fake markers before publishing.

findings.detail:
**Option (a): the public repo is the source of truth and deploys itself.**
- Fits Yu's "move development to public".
- One CI and one provenance chain; /health reports the public SHA. deploy-api.yml already tolerates a live revision that is missing from history and still gates on the journal.
- Free rulesets and branch protection.
- Inferred, not re-verified this session: free standard-runner Actions minutes for public repos.
- Costs: content rulings and a one-time rewrite; an ~120-line live URL sweep; trust re-pointing; a local pre-push relational guard, because GitHub cannot run the private denylist before a public push or PR becomes visible; public logs.

**Option (b): the private repo stays the deploy source and pulls public main plus a private overlay.**
- Keeps migrations and secrets private.
- But it needs sync automation and two CIs. Public CI cannot run tests that need the overlay. /health would show a private SHA, which the public cannot verify. Overlays may only add files, never edit them, or merges conflict.
- Highest ongoing cost.

**Option (c): extend the project-public.ts allowlist projection to the whole tree.**
- Keeps the strongest guard: every publish passes the denylist first. Keeps the release lane unchanged.
- But development stays private, which contradicts Yu's ruling. Every public commit must be a projection commit (`--history`), so public PRs can never merge.
- PRIVATE_ONLY_ROOTS (bin, api, apps, .github, infra, supabase, public) would have to be dismantled.
- It needs the same content rulings as (a), or the projection refuses about 537 files.

findings.recommendation:
Choose (a). Reuse the guard code twice: once as the one-time snapshot gate, and permanently as a pre-push hook plus a scheduled private scan of public main. The private repo keeps:
1. Frozen old main with an archive tag (full history, 103 releases, 119 tags, PR and issue threads).
2. The relational denylist, its allow entries, the guard runner and its private tests.
3. Private overlays: persona and relational docs, dated records such as review/launch-* and docs/superpowers (29 dated files), phase-b tooling, the yutabase fixture job.
4. No deploy secrets. Fly and the survey secret move to a protected environment in the public repo.

Nothing flows from the public repo into the private one except read-only fetches for scanning.
